title: market-sizing-report template variables
description: Values for templates/market-sizing-report.md.j2 and templates/market-sizing-report.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from market-sizing-report.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: Your honest confidence in the SOM figure. If the three methods below disagree by more than about 3x, it is not high, however good the sources for each of them looked.

conversion_assumption.title: Conversion assumption
conversion_assumption.description: The funnel assumptions behind SOM - visitors, signup rate, paid rate - and where each came from. This is the softest input in the document and the one that moves the answer most.

geography_constraint.title: Geography constraint
geography_constraint.description: The geography you can actually sell into and support, with the reason. Language, payment rails and support hours are constraints; "global" is what people write when they have not checked.

industry_constraint.title: Industry constraint
industry_constraint.description: The industry or segment filter applied to reach SAM. Say what it excludes, not just what it includes - the exclusion is the part a reader can check against your product.

market_name.title: Market name
market_name.description: The market or niche being sized, narrow enough to argue about. "Project management software" is a category, not a market - the constraints below only mean something against a real one.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the global figure comes from - publisher, report title, date and URL. Analyst numbers vary by multiples and are frequently circular; an unsourced TAM is a number somebody made up first.
